answers.B: Remove the lesser wing of sphenoid.
answers.C: Remove the ACP (anterior clinoid process).
answers.D: Remove the PCP (posterior clinoid process).
answers.E: Remove optic strut (OS).

questions.explanation: Usually cervical ICA exposure done in patients with a clinoidal ICA aneurysm, a complex or giant aneurysm, or aneurysm of the ophthalmic segment.

questions.question: Paraclinoid aneurysms Anatomy, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Paraclinoid aneurysms are defined as aneurysms arising from the ICA in close proximity to the ACP.
answers.B: The clinoidal segment is usually devoid of named arterial perforators.
answers.C: Paraclinoid aneurysms are classified according to the segment of origin into clinoidal or ophthalmic segment types.
answers.D: The clinoidal segment is located above and laterals to the ACP.
answers.E: The ophthalmic segment is located above and medial to the ACP.

questions.explanation: The clinoidal segment, the distal portion of the anterior ascending vertical segment of the cavernous carotid artery, is located below and medial to the ACP, above the major venous lumen of the cavernous sinus. The ophthalmic segment, the distal portion of the paraclinoid ICA region, lies entirely within the subarachnoid space above and medial to the ACP.

questions.question: Paraclinoid aneurysms Ophthalmic segment, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Ophthalmic segment aneurysms include ophthalmic artery aneurysms and superior hypophyseal artery aneurysms.
answers.B: Ophthalmic artery aneurysm rupture rarely causes SAH.
answers.C: Ophthalmic artery aneurysm causes ipsilateral monocular superior nasal quadrantanopia.
answers.D: Ophthalmic artery aneurysm (when giant) causes ipsilateral near-complete loss of vision and contralateral monocular pie in the sky defect.
answers.E: Hypophyseal artery aneurysms include paraclinoid variant and suprasellar variant.

questions.explanation: Ophthalmic artery aneurysms: These lesions typically arise along the posterior bend of the ICA just distal to the ophthalmic artery and dural ring, project dorsally or dorsomedially, and elevate the lateral edge of the optic nerve against the falciform ligament. The pressure from the falciform ligament against the superior surface of the nerve results in an inferior nasal field defect. Ophthalmic artery aneurysm presentation: 1. 45 % present as SAH. 2. 45 % present as visual field defect: A. As the aneurysm enlarges, it impinges on the lateral portion of the optic nerve which causes inferior temporal fiber compression that causes ipsilateral monocular superior nasal quadrantanopia. B. Continued enlargement causes upward displacement of the nerve against the falciform ligament which causes superior temporal fiber compression that causes monocular inferior nasal quadrantanopia. C. In addition to near-complete loss of vision in the involved eye, compression of the optic nerve near the chiasm may produce a superior temporal quadrant defect in the contralateral eye (junctional scotoma aka “pie in the sky” defect) from injury to the anterior knee of Willebrand (nasal retinal fibers that course anteriorly for a short distance after they decussate in the contralateral optic nerve). 3. 10 % present as both Superior hypophyseal artery aneurysms: There are two main variants: 1. The parasellar variant projects inferiorly toward the sella into the carotid cave, whereas the suprasellar variant projects superiorly into the suprasellar space. Parasellar superior hypophyseal artery aneurysms (also been called carotid cave aneurysms) are usually asymptomatic. 2. Suprasellar or large lesions have a much higher tendency to rupture. When large or giant, these aneurysms tend to elevate the optic chiasm and produce visual changes and relationships to the visual system similar to those seen with pituitary tumors.

questions.question: Paraclinoid aneurysms Ophthalmic and clinoidal segments, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Aneurysms from both of these carotid segments are much more common in males.
answers.B: These segments have a propensity for aneurysm multiplicity.
answers.C: Most paraclinoid aneurysms have a lower rupture risk compared with those at other intracranial subarachnoid sites.
answers.D: Most large (≥1 cm) clinoidal segment aneurysms carry an increased risk for intracranial hemorrhage.
answers.E: Small clinoidal segment aneurysms may be cured with endovascular coiling only.

questions.explanation: Aneurysms from both of these carotid segments are much more common in women, with ratios as high as 9:1 female-to-male predominance. Most present during the fifth and sixth decades of life, usually as either incidental lesions or with mass effect. These segments have a propensity for aneurysm multiplicity; up to half of ophthalmic segment aneurysm patient harbor at least one additional intracranial aneurysm. With the exception of the dorsal variant, which often represents an unstable dissection, most paraclinoid aneurysms have a lower rupture risk compared with those at other intracranial subarachnoid sites. Small asymptomatic aneurysms (<1 cm) are intradural below the subarachnoid space and are therefore generally treated conservatively. Small symptomatic lesions and lesions whose protective ACP roof has been removed for treatment of another aneurysm in the region should be treated. Most large (≥1 cm) clinoidal segment aneurysms have extended through the overlying dural coverings into the subarachnoid space and carry an increased risk for intracranial hemorrhage, and stronger consideration for intervention is therefore given to such lesions even if asymptomatic. Large or giant clinoidal segment lesions often require coiling combined with stenting to achieve satisfactory aneurysm obliteration. Direct surgical obliteration is also a reasonable option but requires broad removal of the ACP and optic strut and opening of the dural ring to gain satisfactory exposure for accurate clip placement. Lesions presenting with epistaxis should be obliterated urgently. Many small unruptured ophthalmic segment lesions appear to have very low risk for rupture, particularly the parasellar superior hypophyseal artery variant, and conservative or endovascular treatment is often preferable to surgery, particularly in older patients with higher surgical risks. When surgery is done, early sectioning of the falciform ligament is helpful to prevent iatrogenic optic nerve injury.

questions.question: Paraclinoid aneurysms Ophthalmic segment, operative technique, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Anterior clinoidectomy has great value in the surgical exposure for most paraclinoid aneurysms.
answers.B: The extradural anterior clinoidectomy is preferable.
answers.C: The risk of damaging the adjacent perforating branches is less in clipping an ophthalmic aneurysm than at other sites on the ICA.
answers.D: The origin of the ophthalmic artery is difficult to expose because of its short intradural length and its location under the optic nerve.
answers.E: Perforator injury during superior hypophyseal artery aneurysm clipping can lead to visual loss.

questions.explanation: The intradural anterior clinoidectomy is preferable in most instances because it allows the surgeon to see the optic nerve and aneurysm during the entire dissection. The risk of damaging the adjacent perforating branches is less in clipping an ophthalmic aneurysm than at other sites on the ICA because ophthalmic aneurysms typically point upward, away from these perforating branches. Perforator injury during superior hypophyseal artery aneurysm clipping can lead to visual loss, so most superior hypophyseal artery aneurysms are best clipped using fenestrated clips.

questions.question: Paraclinoid aneurysms Surgery, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The AChA is seen before the Pcom, although the AChA arises after to the Pcom.
answers.B: The AChA is seen before because the supraclinoidal ICA passes in more lateral direction.
answers.C: The AChA is seen before because it arises further laterally on the posterior wall of the carotid than the Pcom.
answers.D: AChA arises proximal to the Pcom.
answers.E: The AChA pursues a more lateral course than the Pcom.

questions.explanation: In exposing the carotid artery beyond the origin of the ophthalmic artery, the surgeon often sees the AChA before the Pcom, although the AChA arises distal to the Pcom. This occurs because of three sets of anatomic circumstances. 1. First, the supraclinoid segment of the ICA passes upward in a posterolateral direction, placing the origin of the more distally arising branch, the AChA, and further lateral to the midline than the origin of the Pcom, which arises more proximally. 2. Second, the AChA arises further laterally on the posterior wall of the carotid than the Pcom. 3. Third, the AChA pursues a more lateral course than the Pcom; the former passes laterally below the optic tract, around the cerebral peduncle, and into the temporal horn, whereas the latter is directed in a posteromedial direction above and medial to the oculomotor nerve toward the interpeduncular fossa. Care should be taken to preserve both the Pcom and the AChA at the time of obliteration of ICA aneurysms. Occlusion of either of these arteries may cause a hemiplegia, homonymous hemianopia, and reduced levels of consciousness.

questions.question: Paraclinoid aneurysms Post-op visual complication, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Visual symptoms are worsened in 0–8 % after surgical clipping.
answers.B: Visual symptoms improved in 50–74 % after surgical clipping.
answers.C: The cause of worsened vision is vascular in most of the cases.
answers.D: Mechanical injury may occur from manipulation of the optic nerve against the falciform ligament.
answers.E: Thermal injury can occur during drilling of the anterior clinoid process.

questions.explanation: The cause of worsened vision can be mechanical, thermal, or rarely vascular (perforator injury). Visual symptoms improved in 50–74 %, remained stable in 26–42 %, and are worsened in 0–8 % after surgical clipping.

questions.question: Paraclinoid aneurysms* Carotid cave aneurysms, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The carotid cave is a short downward pouching, extends a variable distance below the level of the upper dural ring of the ICA.
answers.B: The carotid cave is most prominent on the posterolateral side of the ICA.
answers.C: Carotid cave aneurysms are those located above the upper ring, but extending into the cave adjacent the upper ring.
answers.D: If the aneurysm arises in the carotid cave, the fundus will extend upward out of the carotid cave on the anteromedial aspect of the ICA.
answers.E: The cave seems to become less prominent as the arteries elongate with advancing age.

questions.explanation: The carotid cave is most prominent on the anteromedial side of the ICA. The upper ring forms a tight collar around the artery, but inspection under the operating microscope reveals that there is often a narrow depression in the dura at the site at which the ring hugs the anteromedial aspect of the artery, called the carotid cave. Carotid cave aneurysms are distinct from clinoid segment aneurysms, which arise from the clinoid segment of the ICA located between the upper and lower dural ring. Aneurysms that arise from the clinoid segment of the ICA have been referred to as clinoid segment aneurysms, and those located above the upper ring, but extending into the cave adjacent the upper ring, are referred to as carotid cave aneurysms.

questions.question: POSTERIOR COMMUNICATING (Pcom) aneurysms Anatomy, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The communicating segment of the ICA begins just below the Pcom artery and ends at the bifurcation.
answers.B: Two major arterial branches (the Pcom artery and the AChA) arise from communicating segment.
answers.C: The Pcom arises from the posteromedial surface of the ICA.
answers.D: The Pcom courses below and lateral to the oculomotor nerve.
answers.E: The Pcom joins the PCA at the junction of the P1 and P2 segments.

questions.explanation: The Pcom courses medially and inferiorly, through the membrane of Liliequist, above and medial to the oculomotor nerve.

questions.question: Pcom aneurysms Anatomy, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Multiple perforators arise from the Pcom and are named the anterior thalamic perforators.
answers.B: These perforators can be stuck to the aneurysm.
answers.C: These perforators should not be clipped with the aneurysm.
answers.D: In about 20 % of patients, there is fetal origin of PCA.
answers.E: In case of fetal origin, the Pcom can be sacrificed.

questions.explanation: In case of fetal origin, the Pcom cannot be sacrificed, and the aneurysm must be clipped in a way to guarantee patency of the parent vessel. In about 20 % of patients, the P1 segment of the PCA is hypoplastic, and the PCA arises directly from the Pcom. This is called fetal origin of PCA.

questions.question: Pcom aneurysms Anatomy, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The typical Pcom aneurysm arises just distal to the origin of the artery from the wall of the ICA and hence is classified as an ICA aneurysm.
answers.B: The Pcom aneurysm projects posteriorly, laterally, and slightly inferiorly and may pinch the oculomotor nerve as it enters the dural fold of cavernous sinus.
answers.C: The third nerve palsy usually occurs with an acutely expanded Pcom aneurysm.
answers.D: RAH is the most important branch associated with Pcom aneurysms.
answers.E: AChA is lying adjacent to the distal neck.

questions.explanation: AChA is the most important branch associated with Pcom aneurysms, lying adjacent to the distal neck. The general rule is to preserve the Pcom and the fetal Pcom; however, if the preoperative angiogram ensures the absence of ipsilateral fetal origin of the PCA and confirms filling of the artery from the posterior circulation, the origin of the Pcom may be included in the clip (if there is no other alternative). This is followed by a second clip applied between the aneurysm and the first thalamoperforators.

questions.question: Pcom aneurysms Presentation, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: More common in females.
answers.B: They usually cause symptoms when larger than 10 mm in patients with SAH.
answers.C: They usually cause IVH into the temporal horn.
answers.D: They could expand and compress the third cranial nerve, causing painful non-pupil-sparing oculomotor nerve palsy.
answers.E: The likelihood of rupture for Pcom is higher than that associated with posterior circulation aneurysms.

questions.explanation: The International Study of Unruptured Intracranial Aneurysms (ISUIA) has shown a likelihood of rupture for this location, similar to that associated with posterior circulation aneurysms. Third nerve palsy following SAH or rapid expansion of a Pcom aneurysm usually resolves completely after 3 months in up to 90 % of patients and resolves partially in the remaining 10 %.

questions.question: Pcom aneurysms Surgical principles, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Avoid temporal lobe retraction because this may avulse an aneurysm stuck to the temporal lobe.
answers.B: The clip blades usually risk both AChA and trochlear nerve.
answers.C: Must identify the AChA.
answers.D: The ICA should not be retracted medially away from the aneurysm because this may rupture an adherent dome.
answers.E: Ensure that the clip blades are not too long to prevent oculomotor nerve injury.

questions.explanation: The clip blades usually risk both AChA and oculomotor nerve.

questions.question: ANTERIOR CHOROIDALARTERY (AChA) aneurysms Anatomy, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: According to the Bouthillier classification of ICA segments, aneurysms of the AChA arise from the C7 segment, which is also called the posterior communicating segment.
answers.B: According to commonly used classification, AChA arises from choroidal segment, which begins at the takeoff of the AChA and ends at the carotid bifurcation.
answers.C: AChA arises proximal and lateral to the Pcom.
answers.D: AChA following course of the optic tract.
answers.E: The main trunk of AChA continues posteriorly, inferior to the optic tract, to enter the choroid fissure.

questions.explanation: AChA arises distal and lateral to the Pcom. AChA has a characteristic course, swinging initially laterally and then posteriorly, following the optic tract and supplying a branch to the mesial temporal structures. The size of this artery is variable, and duplication occurs in as many as 30 % of normal autopsy specimens.

questions.question: AChA aneurysms Presentation, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: AChA aneurysms may be difficult to differentiate radiologically from Pcom aneurysm.
answers.B: IVH usually involves the frontal horn.
answers.C: Because of high location of the AChA above the tentorium, cranial nerve deficits are unlikely.
answers.D: Usually, there is a risk for endovascular coiling of the AChA.
answers.E: These aneurysms are often referred for surgical treatment.

questions.explanation: IVH usually involves the temporal horn.

questions.question: AChA aneurysms Operative technique, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Excessive temporal lobe retraction is avoided because it may rip the dome.
answers.B: In 70 % of the cases, the AChA arises as a single trunk.
answers.C: The key to this operation is to preserve the AChA.
answers.D: Occlusion of AChA may lead to contralateral hemiparesis only.
answers.E: There is no reliable technique to confirm the patency of the AChA after clipping.

questions.explanation: Occlusion of AChA artery leads to classic triad of contralateral hemiparesis, hemianopia, and hemisensory deficit. Excessive temporal lobe retraction is avoided because it may rip the dome of the AChA aneurysm, which frequently adheres to the mesial temporal lobe. Unfortunately, there is no reliable technique to confirm the patency of the AChA except for the direct visualization and inspection of flow inside the artery.

questions.question: ICA bifurcation aneurysms Anatomy and presentation, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The bifurcation of the ICA into an ACA and MCA takes place beneath the basal forebrain and the anterior perforated substance.
answers.B: The aneurysm usually points anterosuperiorly.
answers.C: In most cases, the lenticulostriate perforators of the ICA are displaced posteriorly and may be adherent to the aneurysm.
answers.D: Most commonly present with SAH, but they may present with ICH into the basal ganglia, simulating hypertensive hemorrhage.
answers.E: Most are favorable for coiling procedure.

questions.explanation: Most have a broad base, making an unassisted coiling procedure less favorable.

questions.question: ICA bifurcation aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The ICA bifurcation aneurysms constitute 5 % of all intracranial aneurysms with a male predominance.
answers.B: The ICA bifurcation is the commonest site in children, and they have a worse outcome than their adult counterparts.
answers.C: The dome of the aneurysm, which is usually buried into the substance of the basal forebrain, should not be disturbed.
answers.D: A small frontal corticotomy may be performed to facilitate visualization of the lenticulostriate and the recurrent artery of Heubner.
answers.E: Usually, a straight clip or laterally angled straight clip is applied perpendicular to the direction of ACA and MCA.

questions.explanation: The ICA bifurcation is the commonest site in children, and they have a better outcome than their adult counterparts. Multiple aneurysms are seen in 43 % of patients and the most frequent site of another aneurysm is on the MCA. Bilateral ICA bifurcation aneurysms occur in 6 %.

questions.question: Blister aneurysms of ICA* The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The blood blister-like aneurysms are thin-walled, broad-based aneurysms that lack an identifiable neck.
answers.B: They are fragile and can rupture during microsurgery.
answers.C: The diagnosis of these rare aneurysms is crucial before surgery because the strategy for treatment is different from that of saccular aneurysms.
answers.D: They are mostly asymptomatic and do not necessitate treatment.
answers.E: 3D CTA can easily detect these aneurysms.

questions.explanation: They are mostly present with SAH and necessitate treatment. They are fragile and can rupture during microsurgery, causing postoperative rebleeding more frequently than saccular aneurysms.

questions.question: Blister aneurysms of ICA* The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Endovascular embolization is not recommended.
answers.B: They are usually large based and the very loose fibrinous tissue at the dome.
answers.C: Application of an encircling clip is limited, because of possible sacrifice of the perforating vessel.
answers.D: If clipping is not successful, carotid sacrifice by trapping with or without revascularization should be done.
answers.E: The most successful option is wrapping materials alone around the aneurysms.

questions.explanation: The success rate after wrapping alone is low because of the fragility and likelihood of further growth.

questions.question: Anterior cerebral and anterior communicating artery (ACA and Acom) aneurysms Anatomy, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The most important perforator from the ACA segment is the RAH.
answers.B: The RAH arises from the A2 segment in 78 % of cases.
answers.C: The RAH courses anterior or superior to the A1 segment.
answers.D: The RAH will be encountered after the A1 segment on initial retraction of the frontal lobe during surgery in most cases.
answers.E: The length of the RAH is on average twice that of the A1 segment. Its length therefore increases its exposure to injury during surgery.

questions.explanation: The RAH will be encountered before the A1 segment on initial retraction of the frontal lobe during surgery in most cases. The most important perforator from the proximal A2 segment is the medial striate artery, better known as the recurrent artery of Heubner (RAH).

questions.question: ACA and Acom aneurysms Anatomy, the recurrent artery of Heubner, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: It is unique among arteries in that it doubles back on its parent vessel.
answers.B: The RAH supplies the anterior limb of the internal capsule.
answers.C: Injury to RAH typically results in a moderate paresis of the contralateral upper extremity and mild paresis of the contralateral face.
answers.D: Injury to RAH never causing aphasia.
answers.E: It also causes dysfunction of the tongue and palate.

questions.explanation: If the dominant hemisphere is involved, an expressive aphasia may be evident. It also causes dysfunction of the tongue and palate, which can only be documented during a careful swallowing evaluation. In most patients, these deficits tend to resolve completely in a matter of months. It is unique among arteries in that it doubles back on its parent vessel, passing above the carotid bifurcation, before entering the anterior perforated substance. The RAH supplies anterior striatum (caudate nucleus and putamen), a portion of the outer segment of globus pallidus, and anterior limb of internal capsule.

questions.question: Acom aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The Acom aneurysm forms the largest percentage of ruptured aneurysms.
answers.B: Acom and ACA aneurysms are more common in males.
answers.C: These aneurysms are seen in the middle aged.
answers.D: These aneurysms are seen with a peak in the late forties.
answers.E: The “Acom aneurysm syndrome” includes memory disturbance, confabulation, paraparesis, and personality changes.

questions.explanation: Acom and ACA aneurysms are more common in females.

questions.question: Acom aneurysms RADIOLOGY, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: CT alone can lead to diagnosis which is unique for this aneurysm.
answers.B: Characteristic CT scan findings are either SAH mainly in the interhemispheric fissure or a thick clot in the interhemispheric fissure or ICH in the gyrus rectus.
answers.C: IVH is very rare.
answers.D: Acom aneurysm has the highest false-negative rate of angiography of any intracranial aneurysm.
answers.E: Acute hydrocephalus was present in 25 % of patients.

questions.explanation: IVH is seen in up to 79 % of cases, with the blood entering the ventricles from the ICH in about one third of these. SAH in these aneurysms results in blood in the anterior interhemispheric fissure in essentially all cases and is associated with ICH in 63 % of cases. Acom aneurysm has the highest false-negative rate of angiography of any intracranial aneurysm (due to the balanced flow into the Acom from the paired A1 segments, which may prevent filling of the aneurysm by the dye).

questions.question: Acom aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Acom aneurysm complex exhibits considerable anatomic variation like “dominance” of one A1 segment.
answers.B: The aneurysm usually points in the direction of flow, so may be approached best from the dominant A1.
answers.C: When there is large ICH, the approach is from the side of the ICH to remove the clot.
answers.D: The initial dissection occurs on the anterior surface of the A1 segment taking care to avoid the AChA.
answers.E: Gyrus rectus resection is being helpful especially in superiorly oriented aneurysms to visualize both A2.

questions.explanation: The initial dissection then occurs on the anterior surface of the A1 segment taking care to avoid the recurrent artery of Heubner. Acom aneurysm complex exhibits considerable anatomic variation. In particular, “dominance” of one A1 segment (i.e., a large-caliber A1 vessel supplies the aneurysm, whereas the opposite A1 is hypoplastic) is seen. The aneurysm usually points in the direction of flow (i.e., away from the dominant A1 and toward the opposite hemisphere) and so may be approached best from the dominant A1. When there is ICH, particularly one that causes mass effect in the basal-frontal region, the approach is from the side of ICH to remove clot. In the presence of an Acom aneurysm, the paired A1 segments are of unequal diameter in as many as 85 % of cases. The Acom is rarely oriented in a strictly transverse plane and only in 18 % of cases do ACAs enter the interhemispheric fissure side by side. Thus the Acom is usually oriented in an oblique or sagittal plane. Most Acom aneurysms (71.2 %) project into the interhemispheric fissure and only 16 % of all Acom aneurysms has complex, multilobulated projections.

questions.question: Acom aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Superior projecting aneurysm obscures the contralateral A1/A2 junction.
answers.B: Anterior projecting aneurysm obscures the contralateral optic nerve.
answers.C: Posterior projecting aneurysm obscures the takeoff of the contralateral A2.
answers.D: Inferior projecting aneurysm obscures the hypothalamic perforating arteries.
answers.E: Posterior projecting aneurysm obscures the contralateral optic nerve.

questions.explanation: To understand dissection, Acom aneurysms may be classified into one of four projections based on their orientation in true anatomic space: Superior: Aneurysms project into the interhemispheric fissure, and the fundus often obscures the contralateral A1/A2 junction. Fundus depression during microdissection will help identify the contralateral A1 segment. Anterior: these lesions fill the space between the two optic nerves and so may obscure the contralateral optic nerve. Posterior: Aneurysms project both above and below the plane formed by the A2 segments and often obscure the takeoff of the contralateral A2. Fenestrated clips are useful to occlude this type of Acom aneurysm. Inferior: These aneurysms are “under” the Acom in the region of the hypothalamic perforating arteries that arise from the Acom. The Acom complex vessels generally can be defined before clip application; however, these lesions may be dangerous because there is an intimate association with the perforating vessels and a difficult clip angle.

questions.question: Acom aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Microsurgical clip application is the preferred option in the treatment of Acom with anteriorly directed fundi.
answers.B: Endovascular packing is usually selected for Acom with posteriorly directed fundi.
answers.C: Acom are surgically challenging lesions because of their unilateral retrograde arterial supply.
answers.D: Acom are surgically challenging lesions because of their intimate relationship to 11 critical arteries and perforators.
answers.E: Acom are surgically challenging lesions because of their deep and midline location.

questions.explanation: Acom are surgically challenging lesions because of their bilateral antegrade arterial supply. Their intimate relationship to 11 critical arteries and their perforators: Two A1 segments Two A2 segments Two medial striate arteries of Heubner Two orbitofrontal arteries Two frontopolar arteries The Acom There is no other aneurysm intimately associated with as many vessels. Meticulous preservation of all these vessels is the supreme challenge of clipping Acom aneurysms. The Acom typically have only one parent artery (unlike most other intracranial aneurysms). Although Acom aneurysms are midline structures, they are nevertheless best approached through a lateral craniotomy, and both A1 segments have to be exposed early in the dissection to obtain proximal control.

questions.question: Acom aneurysms Operative technique, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Opening of three arachnoid cisterns (carotid, chiasmatic, and lamina terminalis) lead to the Acom.
answers.B: Resection of the gyrus rectus is essential for adequate exposure of most Acom.
answers.C: Opening of the lamina terminalis is better to be done before the aneurysm clipping in all cases.
answers.D: Aneurysms up to 1 cm from the Acom may be approached through a standard pterional craniotomy with partial gyrus rectus resection.
answers.E: Anterior-pointing aneurysms have the most favorable surgical anatomy.

questions.explanation: Opening of the lamina terminalis increases brain relaxation intraoperatively and reduces the incidence of post-SAH chronic hydrocephalus, but may have to be delayed after the aneurysm is clipped because an inferior-pointing aneurysm may obstruct access to the lamina terminalis, or the dome of a posterior-pointing aneurysm may be prematurely decompressed with this maneuver. Anterior-pointing aneurysms have the most favorable anatomy in this respect because the critical infundibular and hypothalamic perforators course in a direction opposite the aneurysm. Aneurysms >1 cm distal to the Acom up to the genu of the corpus callosum, including those of the pericallosal-callosomarginal bifurcation, may be approached surgically by a basal frontal interhemispheric approach via a frontal craniotomy.

questions.question: Acom aneurysms Complications, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The Acom aneurysm is frequently complicated by electrolyte disturbance.
answers.B: The most common electrolyte abnormality in these patients is hypernatremia.
answers.C: The hyponatremia is commonly due to cerebral salt wasting syndrome rather than SIADH.
answers.D: The Acom aneurysm is frequently complicated by cognitive dysfunction.
answers.E: Cognitive dysfunction is usually the result of a focal lesion in the basal forebrain.

questions.explanation: The most common electrolyte abnormality in these patients is hyponatremia.

questions.question: Acom aneurysms Selection criteria for endovascular treatment, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: An absent A1 segment is a reason for concern but not an absolute contraindication to endovascular therapy.
answers.B: Anatomic features associated with complete embolization included small aneurysm size (<10 mm), small neck size (<4 mm), and anterior dome projection.
answers.C: Factors associated with aneurysm recanalization included large size, posterior dome orientation, and incomplete embolization.
answers.D: Endovascular coiling should be selected as the treatment choice for anteriorly directed domes.
answers.E: Higher rates of surgical complication are found with posteriorly projecting domes.

questions.explanation: Endovascular coiling should be selected as the treatment choice for posteriorly directed domes. The only morphologic risk factor associated with microsurgical treatment was aneurysm dome orientation, with higher rates of surgical complication found with posteriorly projecting domes.

questions.question: Acom aneurysms OUTCOME, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Acom have the best surgical outcomes among all anterior circulation aneurysms.
answers.B: The clinical grade of the patient as measured by the Hunt and Hess or WFNS scale is the primary factor that determines the final outcome.
answers.C: Most of the posterosuperior pointing aneurysms presented in poorer grades.
answers.D: Outcome of the posterosuperior pointing aneurysms is usually unsatisfactory.
answers.E: The most important predictor of outcome was a postoperative stroke.

questions.explanation: Acom have worst surgical outcomes among all anterior circulation aneurysms. The majority of patients surgically treated for SAH reported psychosocial and neurobehavioral changes that were disabling for them and burdensome to their family. In comparison most of the anteroinferiorly pointing aneurysms presented in a better grade and the results were satisfactory. About 75 % of poor outcomes were due to a major ischemic stroke.

questions.question: Distal anterior cerebral artery aneurysms (DACA) The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: DACA arise on the ACA or its branches distal to the Acom.
answers.B: They are uncommon pathologic entity.
answers.C: Typically, these aneurysms are giant and narrow neck in conformation.
answers.D: The callosomarginal artery (CMA) is the most common site of DACA.
answers.E: CMA originates most frequently from the A3 segment.

questions.explanation: Typically, these aneurysms are small and broad based in conformation. The callosomarginal artery originates most frequently (2/3 of cases) from the A3 segment, an average of 43 mm from the Acom junction. The frontopolar artery is the second most common site of DACA. And less commonly at the site of origin of orbitofrontal branch of the ACA.

questions.question: DACA The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Giant aneurysms in this region are exceedingly rare.
answers.B: DACA are associated with additional intracerebral aneurysms at rates as high as 20–25 %.
answers.C: DACA are very rarely spontaneous saccular aneurysm.
answers.D: DACA can be mycotic aneurysms.
answers.E: DACA can be traumatic or tumorous aneurysms.

questions.explanation: DACA most commonly are spontaneous saccular aneurysm. In fact, in contrast to typical aneurysms in other anatomic locations, many of the ruptured DACA are found to be less than 5 mm in diameter, and giant aneurysms in this region are exceedingly rare. An additional critical feature of DACA is their common association with additional intracerebral aneurysms, occurring at rates as high as 20–25 % in large series. These other aneurysms are usually found either on the MCA or at the bifurcations of the ICA.

questions.question: DACA The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Traumatic aneurysms are thought to result from shearing forces exerted on the distal pericallosal artery at the lower margin of falx cerebri.
answers.B: Aneurysms that arise from tumor emboli are most commonly in atrial myxomas.
answers.C: These aneurysms are often requiring microsurgical clipping of the neck.
answers.D: These aneurysms are often requiring trapping with vessel sacrifice.
answers.E: The most commonly observed variants in distal ACA anatomy is azygous ACA.

questions.explanation: These aneurysms may not be amenable to classic microsurgical clipping of the neck and often require trapping with vessel sacrifice. The observed variants in distal ACA anatomy include azygous ACA (type I variation), up to 10 % of DACA are associated with an azygous ACA, in which the distal segments of both anterior cerebral arteries are represented by a single common vessel. The presence of azygous ACA has significant implications, both in considering the surgical approach and in clinical outcome, because damage to the single trunk may result in bihemispheric deficits.

questions.question: DACA CLINICAL PRESENTATION, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The average age at presentation of patients with DACA is about 50 years.
answers.B: DACA appears to have a slight female preponderance.
answers.C: Patients with a ruptured DACA present with classic findings of SAH.
answers.D: ICH is very rare complication of ruptured DACA.
answers.E: All patients with ruptured DACA should search for additional aneurysms.

questions.explanation: ICH is a common complication of ruptured DACA and may be found in as many as 50 % of cases. SAH (which is often prominent in the interhemispheric fissure across the top of the corpus callosum). All patients with suspected ruptured DACA should undergo four-vessel angiography in an attempt to identify the ruptured aneurysm as well as to uncover additional aneurysms.

questions.question: DACA MANAGEMENT, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: DACA are often treated microsurgically because of their peripheral location, small size.
answers.B: DACA are often treated microsurgically because of their unfavorable neck-to-parent artery ratio, tendency to “blow out” the bifurcation at which they occur.
answers.C: The amount of brain retraction needed to clip these lesions is more than other aneurysms.
answers.D: Factors that favor endovascular treatment include extreme age, significant medical comorbidities, poor neurological condition, and irreversible coagulopathy.
answers.E: Proximal arterial control is always achieved later with approach to DACA than with traditional skull base approaches.

questions.explanation: The amount of brain retraction and muscle dissection needed to clip these lesions is comparatively minimal relative to other aneurysms.

questions.question: Middle cerebral artery (MCA) aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The MCA is the third most common location of all intracranial aneurysms.
answers.B: The MCA usually arise at the M1/M2 junction.
answers.C: MCA aneurysms are unique because they may grow to 20 mm before detection.
answers.D: MCA aneurysms are unique because they are more likely to present with IVH.
answers.E: MCA aneurysms are unique because they are more likely to cause symptoms of mass effect than most other intracranial aneurysms.

questions.explanation: MCA aneurysms are unique because they are more likely to present with an ICH. The MCA is the third most common location of all intracranial aneurysms (about 20 %) and usually arises at the M1/M2 junction, projecting laterally in the plane of the M1 segment. They, by virtue of their angioarchitecture, are more challenging to treat with endovascular techniques than other aneurysms within the intracranial circulation.

questions.question: MCA aneurysms Anatomy, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Lying within the sylvian fissure, the MCA is the largest structure.
answers.B: MCA has the most variable anatomy of the all intracranial arteries.
answers.C: MCA is divided into five segments.
answers.D: The M1 has multiple lenticulostriate arteries that are divided into medial and lateral lenticulostriate arteries.
answers.E: The medial lenticulostriate arteries supply the lentiform nucleus, the caudate, and the internal capsule. F. The lateral lenticulostriate arteries supply the caudate nucleus.

questions.explanation: MCA is divided into four segments: M1 (sphenoidal), M2 (insular), M3 (opercular), and M4 (cortical). The medial lenticulostriate arteries enter the anterior perforating substance superiorly and supply the lentiform nucleus, the caudate, and the internal capsule. The lateral lenticulostriate arteries are more variable in their location, traverse the basal ganglia, and supply the caudate nucleus.

questions.question: MCA aneurysms Classification by morphology, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Saccular aneurysms are the most commonly encountered.
answers.B: Fusiform aneurysms can be encountered in MCA but less than saccular aneurysms.
answers.C: Blister aneurysms are more commonly described in the MCA distribution than on the ICA.
answers.D: Extremely dysmorphic or distal aneurysms are usually infectious and are classically identified on distal M4 branches.
answers.E: Bifurcation and trifurcation aneurysms represent up to 90 % of MCA aneurysms.

questions.explanation: Blister aneurysms are less commonly described in the MCA distribution than on the ICA. Bifurcation and trifurcation aneurysms represent up to 90 % of all MCA aneurysms and are the lesions most uniformly referred for surgical consideration.

questions.question: MCA aneurysms Classification by morphology, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Aneurysms of the M1 segment are more common than bifurcation aneurysms.
answers.B: Proximal M1 segment lesions represent 2–12 % of all MCA aneurysms.
answers.C: In patients with multiple intracranial aneurysms, the frequency of proximal MCA aneurysms tends to increase.
answers.D: Nearly three-fourths of patients with multiple intracranial aneurysms harbor an MCA aneurysm.
answers.E: Distal MCA aneurysms are rare and can be either infectious or traumatic.

questions.explanation: Aneurysms of the M1 segment are second in frequency to bifurcation aneurysms and are composed of lenticulostriate or anterior temporal artery saccular aneurysms. Distal MCA aneurysms are the most uncommon of the MCA aneurysms and can be either infectious or, less frequently, traumatic. They also may require a modification of the traditional pterional approach or a different craniotomy entirely. By nature, they are often small and can be challenging to identify; stereotaxis may help facilitate their exposure. Treatment may require trapping and excision, vessel reconstruction, or extracranial intracranial bypass.

questions.question: MCA aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Dissecting MCA aneurysms are rare and may be associated with infection.
answers.B: Traumatic MCA aneurysms are unusual and are most classically associated with a skull fracture.
answers.C: Traumatic MCA aneurysms have a high rupture rate.
answers.D: Traumatic MCA aneurysms are most frequently distal on M3 and M4 segments.
answers.E: Classically, traumatic MCA aneurysms are managed with endovascular coiling.

questions.explanation: Classically, traumatic MCA aneurysms are managed with surgical trapping and excision with or without bypass. Dissecting MCA aneurysms are rare and may be associated with infection, connective tissue diseases such as Marfan’s syndrome, cystic medial degeneration, and fibromuscular dysplasia. Although most present with ischemia, 43 % of patients with an MCA aneurysmal dissection present with SAH, and 75 % of these patients are male. Traumatic MCA aneurysms are most frequently distal on M3 and M4 segments. And often present with delayed rupture (average, 4.7 days) after the inciting trauma.

questions.question: MCA aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Cerebral aneurysms that reach large or giant size are more frequently seen in the MCA distribution than in other arterial distributions.
answers.B: Giant MCA aneurysms represent up to 9 % of MCA aneurysms.
answers.C: Giant MCA aneurysms may become symptomatic without SAH.
answers.D: Giant aneurysms are reported to cause seizures more often than smaller ones.
answers.E: Most M1-lenticulostriate aneurysms are usually giant size.

questions.explanation: Most M1-lenticulostriate aneurysms are quite small (which often precludes endovascular treatment). Classification by size: aneurysms have been somewhat arbitrarily classified by size into small (<5 mm), medium (5–10 mm), large (11–25 mm), and giant (>25 mm). Giant aneurysms are reported to cause seizures more often than smaller ones, and this may be due to mass effect, ischemic changes, or repeated subclinical hemorrhages.

questions.question: MCA aneurysms Management, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Typically, have large sacs containing intraluminal thrombus.
answers.B: The intraluminal thrombus should be left in place without evacuation.
answers.C: Giant aneurysms of the bifurcation that involve one or more of the branches may require vessel sacrifice with flow augmentation.
answers.D: When performing the craniotomy preserve at least one branch of the STA.
answers.E: If a low-flow bypass is anticipated preoperatively, the STA pedicle is dissected out with the opening. F. High-flow extracranial-intracranial may be considered for fusiform aneurysms involving more than one branch.

questions.explanation: Aneurysmorrhaphy: Typically, these large sacs contain intraluminal thrombus that must be removed before clip application. This requires temporary trapping and opening of the sac to evacuate the thrombus. An ultrasonic aspirator is often used to evacuate the intraluminal thrombus more rapidly to reduce temporary occlusion time. Bypass: Most MCA aneurysms can be safely clipped without difficulty and with minimal risk to the afferent or efferent vessels. However, fusiform and giant aneurysms of the bifurcation that involve one or more of the branches may require vessel sacrifice with flow augmentation to properly secure the aneurysm and perfuse the affected brain. When performing the craniotomy for all MCA aneurysms, we preserve at least one branch of the STA in the event an unanticipated STA-MCA bypass is needed. High-flow extracranial-intracranial bypasses using a saphenous vein or radial artery graft may need to be considered for fusiform aneurysms involving more than one branch when successful clip ligation is considered unlikely without it.

questions.question: MCA aneurysms Approaches, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: MCA aneurysms are preferentially clipped at most cerebrovascular centers.
answers.B: Proximal transsylvian approach carries more risk than distal transsylvian.
answers.C: Proximal transsylvian includes splitting the sylvian fissure medially and following the MCA trunk distally.
answers.D: Distal transsylvian includes following the major divisions proximally to the aneurysm by opening the fissure distally.
answers.E: Superior temporal gyrus (STG) approach: making a small corticotomy in the STG and then subsequently entering the distal portion of the sylvian fissure and following the M2 branches to the aneurysm.

questions.explanation: Proximal transsylvian approach is safer than distal transsylvian because of the early parent vessel control.

questions.question: Vertebral artery, PICA, and vertebro-basilar junction aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Posterior circulation aneurysms (including PICA and basilar aneurysms) account for about 8–9 % of all intracranial aneurysms
answers.B: Non-PICA and basilar posterior circulation aneurysms account for 8 % of all intracranial aneurysms.
answers.C: These aneurysms can pose significant challenges because they arise at a region of the skull base.
answers.D: These aneurysms can pose significant challenges because they occur in close proximity to the brainstem and lower cranial nerves.
answers.E: These aneurysms can pose significant challenges because of the variability in the anatomy of the vertebral artery and PICA.

questions.explanation: Aneurysms from the proximal vertebral artery, the vertebral artery-PICA junction, the distal PICA, and the distal vertebral artery make up 25 % of all posterior circulation aneurysms and 2 % of all intracranial aneurysms.

questions.question: Vertebral artery, PICA, and vertebro-basilar junction aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The incidence of fusiform aneurysms at the vertebro-basilar location, much more frequent than in the anterior circulation.
answers.B: These aneurysms carry a high risk for rebleeding as well as high morbidity and mortality rates.
answers.C: Fatal rebleeding in anterior circulation aneurysms is three times the number in the vertebro-basilar aneurysms.
answers.D: Ruptured vertebral dissecting aneurysms carry a worse prognosis than saccular aneurysms of the same location.
answers.E: Early surgical or endovascular treatment of the ruptured aneurysm is generally the rule.

questions.explanation: Fatal rebleeding in 10 % of vertebro-basilar aneurysms, three times the number in their anterior circulation aneurysm group. Vertebral dissections to account for 28 % of posterior circulation aneurysms with rebleeding rate from ruptured dissecting aneurysms has been reported to be 21–71 %.

questions.question: Vertebral artery, PICA, and vertebro-basilar junction aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The most frequent clinical presentation of these aneurysms is SAH.
answers.B: Unruptured aneurysms often present with signs and symptoms of ischemia or mass effect.
answers.C: Angiography is the “gold standard” for diagnosis of vertebral dissection.
answers.D: The vertebral dissection angiographic findings are string sign or rosette sign.
answers.E: The vertebral dissection angiographic findings are pearl sign or double-lumen sign.

questions.explanation: The most frequent clinical presentation of these aneurysms is ICH. The vertebral dissection angiographic findings are string sign, rosette sign, pearl sign, tapered narrowing, occlusion, double lumen, or pseudoaneurysm. Suspicious cases of SAH in which no aneurysm or dissection is detected by CTA are followed up with a conventional four-vessel angiogram with rotational angiography and three-dimensional reconstructions as needed.

questions.question: Vertebral artery, PICA, and vertebro-basilar junction aneurysms (preoperative planning) The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Should include careful attention to the presence of duplicated PICA
answers.B: Should include careful attention to the location of the ipsilateral PICA only
answers.C: Should include whether the PICA territory is supplied by an alternative vessel (such as the AICA)
answers.D: Should include to what degree the posterior cerebral arteries are being supplied through the posterior circulation
answers.E: Should include careful attention to the presence of fetal posterior cerebral arteries

questions.explanation: Should include careful attention to the location of both PICA and especially to the contralateral PICA

questions.question: Vertebral artery, PICA, and vertebro-basilar junction aneurysms* The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: For vertebral artery, PICA, and vertebro-basilar aneurysms, the most widely used are lateral suboccipital or far-lateral suboccipital approaches.
answers.B: Midline suboccipital or paramedian suboccipital approaches are used for more peripheral PICA aneurysms.
answers.C: For peripheral PICA aneurysms located in the tonsillomedullary segment, use the combined lateral and medial suboccipital approach.
answers.D: For PICA aneurysms in the segment distal to the cerebellotonsillar, use a standard midline suboccipital craniectomy extending through the foramen magnum.
answers.E: In far-lateral suboccipital approach, the preferred direction of approach is between the ninth (inferiorly) and the seventh and eighth cranial nerves (superiorly).

questions.explanation: In far-lateral suboccipital approach, the preferred direction of approach is in the space between the 11th inferiorly and the 9th and 10th cranial nerves superiorly. Most PICA aneurysms project superiorly according to Rhoton’s third rule. Rhoton’s third rule: Saccular aneurysms point in the direction that the blood would have gone if the curve at the aneurysm site were not present. The aneurysm dome or fundus points in the direction of the maximal hemodynamic thrust in the pre-aneurysmal segment of the parent artery. Tandem clipping is common with PICA aneurysms because the far-lateral approach provides a view along the axis of the VA, the aneurysms project superiorly, and the PICA often originates from the aneurysm base. In unusually high vertebro-basilar junction aneurysms, use the combined subtemporal-presigmoid transtentorial approach (the vertebro-basilar junction can be accessed by a window formed between the seventh and eighth nerves superiorly and the lower cranial nerves inferiorly). Treatment of vertebral dissecting and fusiform aneurysms: surgical treatments include proximal or parent artery occlusion (Hunterian ligation), trapping procedures, and clip reconstructions. Endovascular options include parent vessel occlusion, stent placement, and combinations of coil and stent therapies, in which the ipsilateral vertebral artery proximal to the aneurysm is occluded. This occlusion can be accomplished through a direct surgical approach by clipping the vertebral artery or by endovascular occlusions using balloons or coils.

questions.question: Basilar trunk aneurysms (BTA) The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: BTAs are those located between the vertebro-basilar junction (VBJ) and the takeoff of the SCAs.
answers.B: The origin of AICA is a common site.
answers.C: More severe clinical sequelae are frequently observed after aneurysm rupture in this region.
answers.D: The severe clinical sequelae include syncope, coma, and death.
answers.E: The mortality rate associated with ruptured BTAs is around 0.3 %.

questions.explanation: The mortality rate associated with ruptured BTAs remains high, around 30 %. The origin of AICA is a common site for many of these aneurysms and is therefore also frequently referred to in order to distinguish upper BTAs (those located between AICA and SCA) from lower BTAs (those located between the AICA and VBJ).

questions.question: Basilar trunk aneurysms Presentation, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Unruptured BTAs frequently present secondary to mass effect on brainstem and the related cranial nerves.
answers.B: Usually aneurysms of the basilar apex, SCA, and upper basilar trunk may result in oculomotor nerve paresis.
answers.C: Middle BTAs in the region of the AICA may result in abducent nerve paresis, facial nerve paresis, or hearing loss.
answers.D: Those located at the VBJ may present secondary to mass effect on the fifth cranial nerve.
answers.E: Signs of brainstem compression, such as hemiparesis, hemisensory deficits, and gait imbalance, may result from mass effect of unruptured BTAs.

questions.explanation: Those located at the VBJ may present secondary to mass effect on the 9th, 10th, and 11th cranial nerves.

questions.question: Basilar trunk aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The mean length of the basilar artery is 30 mm.
answers.B: The mean diameter of the basilar artery is 3–4 mm.
answers.C: The size of the Pcom will not reflect the patient’s ability to tolerate complete parent artery occlusion.
answers.D: Complex or fusiform BTAs may not be amenable to clip ligation or direct aneurysm coiling.
answers.E: Complex or fusiform BTAs may require endovascular occlusion of the parent basilar artery.

questions.explanation: The size of the Pcom is an important prognostic factor in determining a patient’s ability to tolerate complete parent artery occlusion. A balloon occlusion test is performed before complete occlusion, in which multiple modalities are used to demonstrate that the basilar artery can be safely occluded without evidence of brainstem ischemia. More recently, stent-assisted coiling for BTAs has been used.

questions.question: Basilar trunk aneurysms APPROACH selection, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The relationship of the basilar apex to the foramen magnum is a major factor in the preoperative planning of such aneurysms.
answers.B: Aneurysms <18 mm below sellar floor and small/medium sized favoring subtemporal transtentorial approach.
answers.C: Midline aneurysms lying >18 mm below sellar floor or large aneurysms of basilar trunk or vertebro-basilar junction favoring combined supra-infratentorial (petrosal) approach.
answers.D: Aneurysms lying >18 mm below sellar floor, small aneurysms of basilar trunk or vertebro-basilar junction and anteriorly arising tentorial origin of a dominant vein of Labbe on side of approach favoring lateral suboccipital or transcondylar approaches.
answers.E: Subtemporal and petrosal (combined supra/infratentorial) approaches risk damage to the vein of Labbe.

questions.explanation: The relationship of the basilar apex to the dorsum sella is a major factor in the preoperative planning of such aneurysms.

questions.question: Basilar trunk aneurysms* APPROACH selection, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Upper BTAs can be treated with a standard pterional or OZ approach.
answers.B: The transoral-transclival approach has also been used to treat aneurysms of the lower basilar trunk and VBJ.
answers.C: The transoral-transclival approach carries a great risk of transtentorial herniation.
answers.D: Temporary proximal balloon occlusion offers the benefits of proximal control before initiation of the exposure.
answers.E: Balloon occlusion may be used as a transient measure to test whether the basilar artery can be permanently occluded.

questions.explanation: The transoral-transclival approach has also been used to treat aneurysms of the lower basilar trunk and VBJ, yet carries a great risk of CSF leak and meningitis. Temporary proximal balloon occlusion offers the benefits of proximal control before initiation of the exposure, avoidance of obstruction of the operative field by the temporary clip, and ability to confirm occlusion of the aneurysm sac with digital subtraction angiography. Endovascular balloon occlusion testing can be used in conjunction with neuroleptic anesthesia, SPECT imaging, and neurophysiologic monitoring to determine the safety and feasibility of a planned complete occlusion.

questions.question: Basilar apex (bifurcation) (tip) aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Basilar apex account for about half of posterior circulation aneurysms.
answers.B: In basilar apex, the more posterior the aneurysm, the poorer the prognosis.
answers.C: The interpeduncular cistern is enclosed by clivus and posterior clinoid process anteriorly, medial aspects of temporal lobes, and tentorium laterally.
answers.D: Membrane of Liliequist forms posterior boundary of interpeduncular cistern.
answers.E: The interpeduncular cistern is enclosed by the cerebral peduncles posteriorly, and the mammillary bodies and posterior perforated substance superiorly.

questions.explanation: Membrane of Liliequist forms an anterior “curtain” for the interpeduncular cistern. This membrane is a thick layer of arachnoid that anchors from the mammillary bodies superiorly and extends anteriorly and inferiorly before folding posteriorly to form the roof of the prepontine cistern. In basilar bifurcation aneurysms, the more posterior the aneurysm, the poorer the prognosis, because the tendency for vital perforators to be involved becomes greater as the aneurysm projects more posteriorly.

questions.question: Basilar apex aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The terminal basilar artery lies about 15 mm posterior to the posterior aspect of the ICAs.
answers.B: Basilar apex can be located above, below, or at the level of the dorsum sellae.
answers.C: The size of the P1 segment of the PCA depends on the extent to which the Pcom contributes to blood flow in the distal PCA.
answers.D: The cranial nerve most intimately associated with basilar apex aneurysms is the trochlear nerve.
answers.E: Preservation of the posterior thalamoperforating arteries is an essential technical nuance of basilar apex aneurysm surgery.

questions.explanation: The cranial nerve most intimately associated with basilar apex aneurysms is the oculomotor nerve that traverses the space between the PCA and the SCA within the interpeduncular cistern. The size of the segment of the PCA from the basilar bifurcation to the junction with the Pcom (P1) depends on the extent to which the Pcom contributes to blood flow in the distal PCA. A fetal PCA implies that the P1 is a vestigial band, with all PCA blood flow originating from the carotid artery. Preservation of the thalamoperforating arteries is an essential technical nuance of basilar apex aneurysm surgery. These critical perforators arise from the posterior aspect of the basilar trunk, the proximal P1 segments, and the posterior communicating arteries.

questions.question: Basilar apex aneurysms Approach, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The two pure approaches for basilar apex aneurysms are the subtemporal approach and the transsylvian approach.
answers.B: Fundus pointing posteriorly and low basilar bifurcation are favoring subtemporal approach.
answers.C: High basilar bifurcation and narrow neck are favoring transsylvian approach.
answers.D: The presence of other anterior circulation aneurysms on the side of approach is favoring transsylvian pterional approach.
answers.E: In pure transsylvian approach, proximal control is very complicated.

questions.explanation: In pure transsylvian approach, proximal control is straightforward. Also see comments on the next question.

questions.printed_answer_line: v The answer is D. The field is narrow.
questions.question: Basilar apex aneurysms Subtemporal approach, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Offers proximal control is easy.
answers.B: The lateral view facilitates dissection of the perforators.
answers.C: Exposure and clipping of anteriorly or posteriorly directed aneurysms are more feasible than with the transsylvian approach.
answers.D: The field is very wide.
answers.E: Intraoperative bleeding can be difficult to control.

questions.explanation: The field is narrow. The pure transsylvian approach has several assets: 1. Neurosurgeons are familiar with this approach because it is used for more common aneurysms and tumors. 2. Proximal control is straightforward. 3. Exposure of both P1 segments for temporary trapping is uncomplicated. 4. Wide exposure is possible. The transsylvian exposure also has liabilities: 1. Exposure of posteriorly located perforators is difficult. 2. Inspection of distal aspect of clip blade is difficult. 3. Technical features make treatment of directly anteriorly or directly posteriorly projecting aneurysms very difficult. The subtemporal approach offers the surgeon many assets: 1. Proximal control is easy. 2. The lateral view facilitates dissection of the perforators. 3. Tentorial division allows exposure of the upper one-third of the clivus for low-lying bifurcations. 4. Fenestrated clips can be placed with excellent visualization of the thalamoperforators. 5. Exposure and clipping of anteriorly or posteriorly directed aneurysms are more feasible than with the transsylvian. The subtemporal exposure also has liabilities: 1. The field is narrow. 2. Access to the proximal contralateral P1 for temporary trapping is poor. 3. The temporal lobe can be injured in fresh SAH in poor-grade or obese patients. 4. Cranial nerve III palsy often occurs postoperatively (usually transient). 5. Intraoperative bleeding can be difficult to control.

questions.question: Basilar apex aneurysms Pterional approach, the TRUE answer is:

answers.A: PAVEL means pterional approach via the extended lateral corridor.
answers.B: Lateral dissection plane and clipping are better from the surgeon’s dominant side.
answers.C: If patient has right hemiparesis or left oculomotor palsy, the approach must be from the right side.
answers.D: The surgical field is centered on cranial nerve III.
answers.E: Risks include oculomotor palsy in 30 % which is usually temporary.

questions.explanation: If patient has right hemiparesis or left oculomotor palsy, the approach must be from the left side. Pterional approach via the extended lateral corridor (PAVEL) The essential elements of PAVEL include the following: 1. It is performed from the surgeon’s dominant side, which facilitates a due lateral dissection plane and clipping. 2. Wide opening of the sylvian fissure is possible. 3. The surgical field is centered on cranial nerve III. 4. Mesial temporal lobe structures are elevated out of the incisura to the level of the cerebral peduncle. 5. Posterior dissection is performed behind and below ipsilateral P1, not through the neck. 6. The initial clip is fenestrated with a very small blade to close the contralateral neck. 7. The final clip is a short, conventional clip to eliminate residual neck filling through the fenestration. Pterional approach is from the right unless: 1. Additional left-sided aneurysm (e.g., Pcom aneurysm) which could be treated simultaneously by a left-sided approach. 2. Aneurysm points to the right. 3. Aneurysm is located to the left of midline (the operation is more difficult when the aneurysm is even just 2–3 mm contralateral to the craniotomy). 4. Patient has right hemiparesis or left oculomotor palsy.

questions.question: Basilar apex aneurysms TIMING OF TREATMENT, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The peak incidence of repeat hemorrhage after SAH occurs in the first 48 h.
answers.B: Early surgery after SAH avoids the morbidity and mortality associated with repeat hemorrhage.
answers.C: It has been better to do early surgery in the high-grade Hunt and Hess patient.
answers.D: Frequently endovascular treatment is considered for patients with high clinical grades.
answers.E: Of the various approaches, the subtemporal approach is particularly not well tolerated soon after hemorrhage in the high-grade patient.

questions.explanation: It has been better to delay surgery in the high-grade patient (i.e., Hunt and Hess grades IV and V) for a few days unless acceptable occlusion with endovascular therapy is feasible. The peak incidence of vasospasm occurs 7–10 days after SAH. Early surgery after SAH avoids the morbidity and mortality associated with repeat hemorrhage and allows aggressive medical and interventional management of vasospasm. However, certain patients with basilar apex aneurysms may be harmed by early surgery. Occasionally aminocaproic acid is used in patients for whom we delay surgery, particularly if the subarachnoid portion of the bleeding is modest. Proximal occlusion and trapping have important roles in basilar apex aneurysm surgery. To achieve complete aneurysm occlusion safely in a high percentage of patients, coiling should be limited to small aneurysms with neck sizes less than 4 mm and PCAs that do not originate from the dome.

questions.question: Intracranial aneurysms Endovascular approaches, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Balloon remodeling is more often used to Pcom than for Acom aneurysms.
answers.B: Coiling remains the endovascular treatment of choice for MCA aneurysms.
answers.C: Inferiorly and posteriorly projecting Acom are more difficult to coil.
answers.D: Difficult coiling is usually due to suboptimal visualization and catheter instability within the aneurysm.
answers.E: Pericallosal aneurysms are frequently amenable to coil embolization.

questions.explanation: Coiling remains the endovascular treatment of choice for Acom aneurysms.

questions.question: Intracranial aneurysms Endovascular approaches, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Once the anatomic characteristics of the Pcom have been delineated, coil embolization of these lesions is typically straightforward.
answers.B: Unlike Pcom, ophthalmic aneurysms are difficult to be managed through endovascular techniques.
answers.C: Cavernous aneurysms treated by detachable balloon embolization of the aneurysm and later by the advent of aneurysm coiling.
answers.D: MCA aneurysm particularly challenging for endovascular treatment.
answers.E: The relatively small caliber of the MCA compared with the proximal ICA increases the risk of complications.

questions.explanation: Like Pcom aneurysms, ophthalmic aneurysms are easily managed through endovascular techniques. MCA aneurysm particularly challenging for endovascular treatment. Compromise of any of the MCA branches by the coil mass risks a devastating ischemic or thromboembolic insult.

questions.question: Intracranial aneurysms* Endovascular approaches, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Balloon remodeling of PICA is challenging.
answers.B: Balloon remodeling of PICA may require trans-circulation navigation of the balloon from the contralateral vertebral artery.
answers.C: Endovascular techniques are not suited for treatment of PICA aneurysms.
answers.D: Treatment of choice for PCA is endovascular embolization.
answers.E: Balloon and stent-assisted techniques are often mandatory for the treatment of PCA aneurysms.

questions.explanation: Endovascular techniques are ideally suited for the treatment of PICA aneurysms, which are difficult to approach surgically. Because of the difficulty of directly approaching PCA aneurysms microsurgically, the treatment of choice is endovascular embolization.

questions.question: Intracranial aneurysms* Endovascular stenting, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The basic principles underlying stent-supported aneurysm therapy are parent vessel protection and parent vessel remodeling.
answers.B: Parent vessel protection prevents coil embolization.
answers.C: Parent vessel remodeling includes stents that produce flow diversion and provide scaffolding for neo-intimal overgrowth.
answers.D: Parent vessel remodeling may facilitate and maintain aneurysm thrombosis.
answers.E: Parent vessel remodeling includes parent vessel configuration, flow redirection, and tissue overgrowth.

questions.explanation: Basic principles underlying stent-supported aneurysm therapy: 1. Parent vessel protection: stents could be applied to provide durable parent vessel protection, facilitating the coil embolization of wide-necked aneurysms by preventing coil prolapse into the parent vessel. 2. Parent vessel remodeling: A. Parent vessel configuration: The implantation of a stent within a parent artery may straighten the vessel, altering (possibly in a favorable manner) the flow dynamics within the aneurysm. The magnitude of this effect is affected primarily by the rigidity of the stent. B. Flow redirection: The presence of stent tines over the aneurysm neck functions to disrupt the inflow jet, reducing vortices and shear stress on the aneurysm wall and reducing the “water-hammer” effect of chronic pulsatile blood flow on an intra-aneurysmal coil mass. The magnitude of this is affected primarily by the amount of metal surface area coverage provided by the stent. C. Tissue overgrowth: the presence of a stent across the neck of the aneurysm provides a scaffolding and stimulus for the overgrowth of endothelial and neo-intimal tissue across the neck of the aneurysm, creating a “biologic remodeling” in the region of the aneurysm neck.

questions.question: Intracranial aneurysms* Endosaccular packing include, FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Endosaccular coil embolization.
answers.B: Balloon-assisted coil embolization.
answers.C: Endosaccular liquid embolic agents.
answers.D: Neck bridge devices.
answers.E: Flow diverters are not included.

questions.explanation: Endosaccular packing includes stent and coils or stent alone (flow diverter).

questions.question: Intracranial aneurysms Recurrence after endovascular treatment, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Neck width >4 mm increases the risk of recurrence.
answers.B: Overall sac size (small < large).
answers.C: Presence of intra-saccular thrombus increases the risk of recurrence.
answers.D: Recurrence rate is 60 % in large/giant dysplastic aneurysms.
answers.E: Recurrence rate is more in small aneurysms with small neck.

questions.explanation: The main factor influencing recurrence after endovascular treatment is the aneurysm sac and neck size. Recurrence rates are 5–10 % in small aneurysms (<10 mm) with small necks (<4 mm), 20 % in small aneurysms with large necks, and 60 % in large/giant dysplastic aneurysms.

questions.question: Treatment of aneurysmal rupture during coiling The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Inflate balloon if balloon-assisted coiling is used.
answers.B: Immediately reverse anticoagulation.
answers.C: Stop packing coils as rapidly as possible.
answers.D: Continue to pack coils as rapidly as possible.
answers.E: Insert an extraventricular drain (EVD).

questions.explanation: Immediately reverse anticoagulation (protamine should be available during the procedure).

questions.question: Intracranial aneurysms Endovascular Hunterian ligation, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: One of the oldest successful interventions for arterial aneurysms.
answers.B: Is permanent sacrifice of parent artery to prevent blood access to aneurysm.
answers.C: This technique has also been referred to as “reconstructive” therapy.
answers.D: Hunterian ligation most often targets complex aneurysms.
answers.E: Hunterian ligation can be used occasionally for vascular tumors.

questions.explanation: This technique has also been referred to as “deconstructive” therapy, in contrast to “reconstructive” therapy, which refers to the targeted occlusion of a vascular abnormality without impairment of blood flow in the parent vessel. One of the oldest successful interventions for arterial aneurysms— ligation of the femoral artery to treat a popliteal aneurysm by John Hunter in 1785. The carotid arteries were the first cerebral vessels to be intentionally and successfully ligated in 1808 by the English surgeon Astley Cooper. Hunterian ligation can be used occasionally for hemorrhagic stroke, vascular tumors, arteriovenous malformations, fistulas, and arterial dissections.

questions.question: Intracranial aneurysms* Endovascular approaches (INDICATIONS), the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Hunterian ligation is reserved primarily for giant and fusiform aneurysms.
answers.B: Some traumatic aneurysms may be candidates.
answers.C: Some infectious aneurysms may be candidates.
answers.D: The current standard of care requires preoperative evaluation with balloon test occlusion.
answers.E: Occlusion of the vertebral artery was most effective at its origin from subclavian artery.

questions.explanation: Occlusion of the vertebral artery was most effective at the level of C1 because antegrade collateral flow is possible through the external carotid artery. The current standard of care requires preoperative evaluation with balloon test occlusion (BTO) followed by distal perfusion. The major treatment question when considering endovascular Hunterian ligation is whether to perform an arterial bypass before permanent vessel occlusion.

questions.question: PICA aneurysms* Endovascular approaches, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: If aneurysm is separated from the origin of PICA, internal occlusion is done.
answers.B: If aneurysm involves the origin of PICA and has SAH, proximal occlusion and internal trapping is preferred.
answers.C: If aneurysm involves the origin of PICA and has no SAH, direct internal occlusion is done.
answers.D: If aneurysm involves the origin of PICA and has no SAH, BTO followed by occipital artery-PICA bypass is preferred.
answers.E: Too much collateral flow can prevent aneurysmal thrombosis.

questions.question: Intracranial aneurysms Complications of endovascular approaches, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Ischemic stroke
answers.B: Post-occlusion thromboembolism
answers.C: Coil migration
answers.D: Secondary AVM development
answers.E: Perforator occlusion

questions.question: Giant intracranial aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Giant aneurysms represent 2–5 % of all intracranial aneurysms.
answers.B: Giant intracranial aneurysms have a minimum diameter of at least 25 mm.
answers.C: Giant aneurysms have a male preponderance.
answers.D: Most patients become symptomatic in the fourth through sixth decades of life.
answers.E: Giant aneurysms currently remain primarily a surgical disease.

questions.explanation: As with other aneurysms, giant aneurysms have a female preponderance. Giant aneurysms currently remain primarily a surgical disease that must be managed effectively to minimize morbidity.

questions.question: Giant intracranial aneurysms The FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Giant aneurysms are found in ACA mainly.
answers.B: Giant aneurysms may result directly from trauma.
answers.C: More than one aneurysm may be present in 10–36 % of patients.
answers.D: A significant proportion of giant aneurysms have associated intraluminal thrombus.
answers.E: The presence of a partially thrombosed aneurysm does not appear to lower the risk for rupture of the aneurysm.

questions.explanation: In general, 34–67 % of giant intracranial aneurysms are associated with the ICA, 11–40 % with the anterior cerebral artery and middle cerebral artery (MCA), and 13–56 % with the vertebral and basilar arteries. A significant proportion of giant aneurysms have associated intraluminal thrombosis—as many as 60 % in some series.

questions.question: Giant intracranial aneurysms Presentation, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Signs and symptoms due to a mass effect develop in approximately two-thirds.
answers.B: Only about a third of patients have SAH as the initial symptom.
answers.C: 7 % of patients with giant aneurysms initially had ischemic symptoms.
answers.D: Annual rupture rate for giant aneurysms is lower than small aneurysms.
answers.E: Annual rupture rate for giant intracranial aneurysms of around 6 %.

questions.explanation: Annual rupture rate for giant intracranial aneurysms of around 6 %, higher than the 1–3 % rate quoted for smaller aneurysms.

questions.question: Giant intracranial aneurysms Management, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: The approaches used for giant aneurysms of the posterior fossa include orbitozygomatic, transpetrosal, or far-lateral approaches.
answers.B: Circulatory arrest permits complete vascular control, but increase the risk for intraoperative rupture of the aneurysm.
answers.C: Hypothermic circulatory arrest can facilitate the surgical technique.
answers.D: The absence of blood flow greatly facilitates clip reconstruction.
answers.E: Endovascular techniques are more preferred for giant cavernous sinus aneurysms.

questions.explanation: Circulatory arrest permits complete vascular control and the risk for intraoperative rupture of the aneurysm is eliminated. Hypothermic circulatory arrest can facilitate the surgical technique by allowing more aggressive manipulation of the aneurysm dome without fear of rupture.

questions.question: Giant intracranial aneurysms Hypothermic circulatory arrest, the FALSE answer is:

answers.A: Deep hypothermia increases the brain’s metabolic requirements for oxygen.
answers.B: During circulatory arrest, adequate cerebral protection with barbiturates is imperative.
answers.C: Hypothermic circulatory arrest is associated with a mortality rate of 8 %.
answers.D: The risks related to hypothermic circulatory arrest include coagulopathies.
answers.E: The risks related to hypothermic circulatory arrest include hemodilution after blood products and intravenous fluids are replaced.

questions.explanation: Deep hypothermia reduces the brain’s metabolic requirements for oxygen. Hypothermic arrest associated with 13 % morbidity and 8 % mortality.
